New York (AP) — Singer Lionel Richie's representatives confirmed to The Associated Press on Wednesday that Richie has paused his concert tour to recover from heart surgery.

The statement said that Richie underwent a common procedure to treat atrial fibrillation (A-fib), that "the surgery went very well," and that "he is recovering nicely, but needs a period of rest, and will be back on stage soon."

Atrial fibrillation is a quivering or irregular heartbeat that can lead to blood clots, stroke and heart failure. Researchers estimate that more than 10 million people in the United States have the condition, mostly older adults.

The 77-year-old singer also postponed two shows in June due to illness. In August, reports circulated online that he had checked himself into a hospital after performing in St. Louis.

Richie was scheduled to perform with Earth, Wind & Fire in San Francisco on Saturday, and was also booked in Chicago on September 30 and Columbus, Ohio on October 3.

According to his official website, he is currently scheduled to begin his "King of Hearts" residency at the Wynn in Las Vegas in October and November.

Richie is an Academy Award winner and a four-time Grammy Award winner. He launched his career with The Commodores and later became a hugely popular solo artist. In addition to hits like "Hello," he co-wrote the classic charity single "We Are the World" with Michael Jackson, which has sold more than 100 million records. He has also served as a judge on American Idol.
